headline: Marmot Population on Vancouver Island Reaches 427
meta_description: Vancouver Island's marmot population has climbed to 427 as dedicated recovery efforts show measurable success in species conservation.
summary_short: Conservation work is paying off as the marmot population on Vancouver Island grows to 427, a milestone in ongoing recovery efforts.
body:
The marmot population on Vancouver Island has climbed to 427, marking steady progress in a long-running species recovery program. This growing number represents hope for a creature once facing extinction on the island, where habitat loss and predation had severely threatened survival.

Recovery efforts have centered on protecting and restoring the unique ecosystem these animals depend on. Each individual marmot counted represents the collective work of conservationists and scientists dedicated to reversing decades of decline. The milestone reflects patience and commitment to a multi-year strategy—the kind of persistent, unglamorous work that rarely makes headlines but fundamentally changes outcomes for endangered species.
quick_facts: Vancouver Island marmot population now stands at 427
Recovery efforts continuing on Vancouver Island
